student_profile.raw_notes: Susan Chartuse is an 11-year-old 5th grade student at Orange Sables Elementary referred for evaluation due to parental concerns regarding possible ADHD and dyslexia. Background history notes early developmental milestones were met at an average rate, with a history of chronic ear infections, tonsillectomy at age eight, and early physical high activity. She was retained in kindergarten. In school, she struggles with reading and math, but excels in creative writing. Behavioral observations during testing revealed a habit of mentally drifting when tasks became challenging, easy discouragement, and decoding issues during reading tasks. Comprehensive testing included the WISC-V, Woodcock-Johnson IV Tests of Cognitive Ability, Oral Language, and Achievement, Conners Parent Rating Scale, Achenbach CBCL, and IVA Continuous Performance Test. Results on the WISC-V revealed a Full Scale IQ of 98 (Average range), with a significant discrepancy between her Verbal Comprehension Index (VCI = 78, Very Low) and Fluid Reasoning Index (FRI = 118, High Average). WJ-IV Achievement testing placed her Broad Reading at grade equivalent 3.1 (percentile rank 7) and Broad Mathematics at grade equivalent 3.5 (percentile rank 5), indicating deficits approximately 2 to 2.5 grade levels behind her placement. Visual processing deficits (Number-Pattern Matching percentile 19) support a diagnosis of dyslexia, while auditory processing and memory functions remain relative strengths. Parent rating scales (Conners T-score 87 for executive functioning, 88 for hyperactivity/impulsivity; CBCL clinical elevation in inattention) and clinical observation support an ADHD diagnosis despite a passing IVA score. Formal DSM-5 diagnoses provided by Dr. Gary M. Eisenberg include Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder - Combined Type, Learning Disorder with impairments in reading, and Learning Disorder with impairments in mathematics. Recommendations include discussing psychostimulant medication with her pediatrician, daily exercise, participation in enjoyable extracurriculars, maintaining self-esteem, and specific IEP accommodations including extra movement breaks during tests, extended test time (1.5x), and testing in a quiet, solitary environment, alongside active reading comprehension strategies like SQR3.
student_profile.academic_history: Susan was retained in kindergarten. By third grade, she had difficulty with multiplication tables, telling time, and coin values. Current testing places her broad reading at 3.1 grade equivalent and broad mathematics at 3.5 grade equivalent.
student_profile.teacher_observations: Preschool teachers noted she would wander off during class, and first-grade teachers reported she could not sit in her seat. During testing, she mentally drifted when work became difficult but was responsive to redirection.
student_profile.parent_concerns: Parents were concerned that Susan may have ADHD or dyslexia, noted difficulty pronouncing words, and reported focus issues delaying homework completion.

drafted_iep.background_info: Susan Chartuse, Date of Birth: May 12, 2015 (Age 11 years). Grade: 5.7, Section B. School: Orange Sables Elementary. Student Registration ID: OSE-2021-8842. Disability Classification: Specific Learning Disability (Moderate) under the RPwD Act 2016 Schedule. Primary Language: English; Secondary Language: Hindi. Date of IEP Team Meeting: July 10, 2026. Date of Service Initiation: July 15, 2026. Parents: Mr. Arthur Chartuse and Mrs. Ellen Chartuse (Contact: +91-9876543210, Email: chartuse.family@email.com). Medical Alerts: Documented history of executive dysfunction, inattention, and physical hyperactivity; no known drug allergies or physical health contraindications.
drafted_iep.academic_performance:
Present Level: Academic/Educational Achievement - Susan is currently functioning below grade level in Broad Reading (Grade Equivalent 3.1) and Broad Mathematics (Grade Equivalent 3.5), while functioning at or above grade level in Creative Writing and oral narrative expression. In reading, Susan exhibits severe decoding deficits and struggles to independently extract main ideas from dense non-fiction text, though her verbal listening comprehension is well developed. In mathematics, calculation speed and multi-step word problem solving are significantly impacted by working memory bottlenecks and task drift.

Present Level: Cognitive Ability - Susan demonstrates a High Average fluid reasoning capacity with a Fluid Reasoning Index of 118 on standardized cognitive assessments, highlighting superior non-verbal problem-solving and conceptual logic skills. Her working memory and processing speed represent relative vulnerabilities that create barriers during fast-paced written instruction.

Present Level: Language Ability & Learning Style - Susan possesses strong auditory processing and auditory memory capabilities relative to her overall profile. She is an auditory-tactile learner who acquires knowledge most effectively when text is supplemented by text-to-speech audio rendering, active reading frameworks (SQ3R), physical movement integration, and structured graphic organizers.

Present Level: Rate of Progress - With standard unaccommodated instruction, Susan's progress fluctuates due to fatigue and decoding barriers. However, when explicit multi-sensory instruction and executive function supports are provided, her rate of skill acquisition in narrative writing and novel mathematical reasoning accelerates rapidly.
drafted_iep.social_development:
Susan is an engaging, expressive, and empathetic student who builds positive relationships with peers and adults. She demonstrates vibrant oral expression and enjoys collaborative creative projects. Present levels indicate that her social interaction skills are age-appropriate, but her fragile academic self-concept in reading and mathematics often leads to self-discouragement, task avoidance, or quick frustration when content becomes dense.

When academic frustration occurs, Susan exhibits a tendency to mentally drift or display impulsive physical movements. Her self-concept improves markedly when her creative writing talents are recognized. She requires proactive emotional check-ins, structured peer buddy systems, and positive behavioral reinforcement to sustain effort, manage academic anxiety, and build resilience during challenging learning activities.
drafted_iep.physical_development:
Susan is a physically healthy 11-year-old child with normal visual and auditory acuity, displaying age-appropriate gross and fine motor skills. Her disability profile of Specific Learning Disabilities (Moderate) is accompanied by documented high physical activity levels, executive dysfunction, and inattention during structured classroom activities.

Susan exhibits no mobility or physical health limitations that restrict participation in general school activities. However, her sensory-motor needs require the integration of structured movement breaks into classroom instruction and formal assessment blocks to manage internal physical restlessness and maintain continuous focus.
drafted_iep.management_needs:
Susan requires a moderate-to-significant level of environmental, material, and human supports across academic settings to access the curriculum. Environmentally, she requires preferential seating near the focal point of instruction away from distractions, visual schedule boards, and access to a separate, quiet, distraction-free environment for all formal evaluations.

Materially, Susan requires text-to-speech (TTS) and speech-to-text (STT) assistive software, structured graphic organizers, visual math cue cards, and multi-sensory instructional frameworks. Humanly, she requires specialized resource room support from a Special Educator (4 sessions per week, 45 minutes each), school counseling support for frustration management (1 session per week, 30 minutes), and regular consultation between her general education teachers and the Special Education Coordinator.
drafted_iep.long_term_outcomes: N/A — Student is 11 years old. Long-term adult outcomes and post-secondary transition planning will be formally developed when the student turns 14 years of age pursuant to RPwD Act 2016 Section 17 and NCTE/NCERT Guidelines.
drafted_iep.annual_goals:
Annual Goal 1: By the end of the academic year, Susan will improve her reading comprehension and decoding skills from a 3.1 grade level equivalent to a 4.2 grade level equivalent using active reading strategies (SQ3R) and multi-sensory instruction across grade-level texts.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Susan will apply the SQ3R reading comprehension framework (Survey, Question, Read, Recite, Review) to 3rd-grade level passages as measured by teacher-scored graphic organizers with 80% accuracy over 3 consecutive trials.
2. By the end of Term 2, Susan will apply SQ3R reading comprehension strategies to 4th-grade level passages utilizing text-to-speech (TTS) assistive technology as measured by teacher-scored graphic organizers with 80% accuracy over 4 consecutive trials.
3. By the end of Term 3, Susan will independently apply SQ3R strategies and correctly answer explicit and inferential comprehension questions on grade-level texts as measured by bi-weekly teacher-made quizzes with 75% accuracy across 3 trials.
Evaluation Procedures: Teacher-made tests, Graphic organizer rubrics, Running reading records
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly

Annual Goal 2: By the end of the academic year, Susan will increase her mathematical calculation and word-problem reasoning skills from a 3.5 grade level equivalent to a 4.5 grade level equivalent using multi-sensory tools and visual problem-solving frameworks.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Susan will solve two-step mathematical word problems involving multi-digit addition and subtraction using structured graphic organizers with 75% accuracy as measured by weekly curriculum-based assessments.
2. By the end of Term 2, Susan will correctly solve multi-step multiplication and division word problems utilizing tactile manipulatives and visual step-by-step cue cards with 80% accuracy over 4 consecutive trials as measured by classroom math rubrics.
3. By the end of Term 3, Susan will solve Grade 5 mathematical word problems involving fractions and decimals using speech-to-text / read-aloud accommodations with 75% accuracy as measured by term math assessments.
Evaluation Procedures: Curriculum-based measures, Math rubric evaluations, Student work samples
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly

Annual Goal 3: By the end of the academic year, Susan will demonstrate enhanced executive functioning and sustained task completion during independent math and reading periods by utilizing self-monitoring tools and scheduled movement breaks.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Susan will complete independent math and reading tasks utilizing scheduled 3-minute movement breaks every 15 minutes as measured by weekly behavioral tracking logs showing a 50% reduction in unmanaged task drift across 4 consecutive weeks.
2. By the end of Term 2, Susan will independently initiate a self-regulation movement break or sensory tool upon recognizing academic frustration in 4 out of 5 observed opportunities as measured by teacher observation checklists.
3. By the end of Term 3, Susan will remain actively engaged in independent academic tasks for 25 consecutive minutes with no more than 1 teacher prompt in 4 out of 5 trials as measured by interval time-sampling data.
Evaluation Procedures: Weekly behavioral tracking logs, Teacher observation checklists, Direct interval timing logs
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly
drafted_iep.special_education_services:
A. Special Education Programs:
- Specialized Resource Room Support (Pull-out / Small Group): Provided by Special Educator, Frequency: 4 sessions per week (45 minutes per session), Initiation Date: July 15, 2026, Duration: Academic Year 2026-2027.
- Counseling / Social-Emotional Support Services: Provided by School Psychologist, Frequency: 1 session per week (30 minutes per session), Initiation Date: July 15, 2026, Duration: Academic Year 2026-2027.

B. Extended School Year Services: No.

C. Supplementary Aids and Modifications (Initiation: July 15, 2026):
- Differentiated UDL-based curricular materials and flexible assessment procedures per NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.30, p.57).
- Specialised reading instruction using explicit, multi-sensory methods (e.g., Orton-Gillingham / VAKT approach).
- Written language support including graphic organisers and structured writing frameworks.
- Structured movement breaks integrated into instruction and assessment per RPwD Act Section 16(iii) reasonable accommodation mandate.
- Preferential seating near the instruction point, away from door/window distractions.

D. Assistive Technology Devices/Services:
- Provision of Text-to-speech (TTS) and Speech-to-text (STT) assistive software (e.g., Immersive Reader, Read&Write) for decoding barriers during reading and composition tasks per RPwD Act Section 17(g) and NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.30).

E. Program Modifications for School Personnel:
- General education teacher consultation / training on disability accommodations provided bi-weekly by the Special Education Coordinator.

F. Individual Testing Modifications:
- Extended time (1.5x / 50% additional time, exceeding minimum 25%) on all tests and examinations per RPwD Act Section 17 and Section 16(ii).
- Separate, quiet, distraction-free room for all assessments (solitary test environment).
- Use of assistive technology (TTS and STT) during examinations.
- Structured movement breaks integrated into assessment sessions.
drafted_iep.general_education_participation:
Susan will participate in the General Education classroom for approximately 75% of the instructional school day. She will fully join her peers in general education settings for Creative Writing, Social Studies, Science, Art, Music, and Physical Education. She will be pulled out for specialized resource room support (4 sessions of 45 minutes per week) during core skill consolidation periods to address reading decoding and math deficits.

Susan will participate fully in all non-academic, co-curricular, and physical education activities with non-disabled peers, utilizing integrated movement strategies. Pursuant to RPwD Act provisions for learning disabilities and CBSE/NCERT guidelines, Susan is recommended for flexible second language provisions (exemption or functional alternative language evaluation). General and special education teachers will collaborate to implement UDL principles across all inclusive classes.
drafted_iep.participating_agencies: N/A — Transition services and participating agency commitments are not applicable at age 11. External agency involvement will be evaluated at age 14 per RPwD Act 2016 requirements.
drafted_iep.coordinated_activities:
1. Instruction: Provision of UDL-based instruction, multi-sensory reading frameworks (SQ3R), explicit math organizers, and integrated assistive technology across general education classes.
2. Related Services: Specialized resource room instruction (4x/week) and school psychological counseling (1x/week) for emotional regulation and frustration tolerance.
3. Employment/Post-secondary Education: N/A at age 11.
4. Community Experience: Full inclusion in school field trips, assemblies, and co-curricular events with movement accommodations and peer support.
5. Activities of Daily Living: Executive function coaching for desk organization, time management, and self-advocacy within the school environment.
6. Functional Vocational Assessment: N/A at age 11.
drafted_iep.recommendations_summary: Disability Classification: Specific Learning Disability (Moderate) with associated Executive Dysfunction, categorized under the RPwD Act 2016 Schedule. Recommended Placement: Inclusive General Education Classroom with resource room support (4 sessions/week, 45 mins each) and school counseling (1 session/week, 30 mins). Extended School Year: Not required at present. Transportation: Standard school bus transport with preferential front seating. Committee Recommendations: Complete implementation of all RPwD Act mandatory accommodations, including 1.5x extended test time, separate quiet testing room, TTS/STT software access, multi-sensory reading instruction, structured movement breaks, and UDL-aligned flexible assessment procedures.
drafted_iep.progress_reporting:
Susan's progress toward her annual IEP goals will be formally reported to her parents at the same frequency as non-disabled peers, following the quarterly reporting cycle (4 times per academic year). Progress reporting will be delivered through written progress reports attached to standard report cards, teacher contact logs, and work sample portfolios.

Progress will be measured using curriculum-based measures, teacher-scored graphic organizer rubrics, behavioral tracking logs, and standardized benchmark assessments. Formal parent-teacher-specialist conferences will be held at the end of each term to discuss progress, review accommodation effectiveness, and adjust goals as necessary.

rpwd_relevant_sections: Section 16(ii): Duty to provide reasonable accommodation according to the individual's requirements
Section 16(iii): Provision of necessary support, individualized or otherwise, in environments that maximize academic and social development
Section 17(g): Provision of suitable pedagogical and technological supports, aids, and assistive devices
ncte_relevant_sections: NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.30): Implementation of UDL-based modified/differentiated curriculum, accessible assessment tools, and adequate provision/frequency of resource persons (specialized therapists/psychologists)
NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.32): Monitoring the nature, frequency, and extent of support required, alongside timely distribution of proper aids, appliances, and assistive devices
NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.57): Key Performance Indicators (KPI 12, 18, 19) for special education/therapeutic support, UDL-based teaching, and flexible assessment procedures
identified_gaps: Missing explicit documentation of the nature, frequency, and duration of support from a Special Education Teacher or Psychologist to address moderate SLD and severe executive dysfunction
Lack of defined UDL-based flexible assessment tools and classroom pedagogical modifications, relying solely on standardized test accommodations rather than continuous inclusive assessment
mandatory_accommodations: Extended time (minimum 25% additional) on all tests and examinations (RPwD Act Section 17)
Separate, quiet, distraction-free room for all assessments (RPwD Act Section 17)
Use of assistive technology: text-to-speech and speech-to-text software
Specialised reading instruction using explicit, multi-sensory methods
Written language support including graphic organisers and structured writing frameworks
General education teacher consultation / training on disability accommodations
Extended testing time (1.5x) and quiet solitary test environment per RPwD Act Section 16(ii)
Provision of Text-to-speech (TTS) and Speech-to-text (STT) assistive software per RPwD Act Section 17(g) and NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.30)
Structured movement breaks integrated into instruction and assessment per RPwD Act Section 16(iii) reasonable accommodation mandate
Differentiated UDL-based curricular materials and flexible assessment procedures per NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.30, p.57)
Access to resource room support and specialized personnel (Special Educator / Psychologist) with designated frequency per NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.30)
compliance_report.compliance_notes: The IEP incorporates critical accommodations such as extended test time, assistive technology, and movement breaks. However, it is rated as 'partial' compliance because it lacks specific details on the frequency and delivery model of specialized resource teacher/psychologist support and fails to formalize UDL-based flexible assessment methods required under NCTE/NCERT Guidelines and RPwD Act Section 16.
